title: Asking the Right Questions

patient.name: Mr Subramaniam s/o Raju
patient.presenting_complaint: Blurred vision in the right eye; here as a walk-in and needs a focused history before being seen

history.hpc: Mr Subramaniam reports blurred vision in the right eye. He says: 'My right eye blur, I not sure when start, on and off.' The PSA must take a focused ocular presenting-problem history to help triage: whether the change was sudden or gradual, partial or total, one or both eyes, with associated flashes, floaters, pain, or redness.
history.social_hx: Security supervisor doing shift work. Wears glasses for reading.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: To be assessed by doctor; history guides urgency

investigations.history_documentation: Focused ocular presenting-problem history taken: onset (sudden vs gradual), partial vs total loss, one or both eyes, blurry vs double vision, any sudden drop, flashes/floaters/headaches, recent surgery or trauma, red/sore/itchy eye, and current correction. The structured history clarifies the complaint and flags any red flags for the doctor.

diagnosis: A focused ocular history clarifies a vague 'blurring' complaint and screens for red flags (e.g., sudden loss, flashes/floaters) that would change urgency, in a diabetic patient. The PSA competency is structured history taking and documentation to support triage; diagnosis is the doctor's.

immediate: Take a structured ocular presenting-problem history: sudden vs gradual, partial vs total, one or both eyes
Ask about blurry vs double vision, any sudden drop, and flashes/floaters/headaches
Ask about recent eye surgery or trauma and any red/sore/itchy eye
Confirm current correction (glasses/contact lenses) and relevant systemic history (diabetes)
Identify any red-flag answers that would raise triage urgency
Document the history clearly and measure VA for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to assess, with the history guiding the focus (e.g., diabetic eye disease)
Triage urgency adjusted if any red flags emerged
Record the history on the patient's record
patient_education: Explain that the questions help the doctor understand and prioritise his problem
Encourage him to mention any sudden changes, flashes, or floaters
Reassure him he will be assessed and advise him to report new symptoms while waiting
Encourage good diabetic control and regular eye checks

key_points: Clarifies onset (sudden vs gradual) and whether one or both eyes
Asks about partial vs total loss and associated flashes/floaters/headaches
Asks about recent surgery/trauma and red/sore/itchy eye
Confirms current correction and relevant systemic history (diabetes)
Uses a structured ocular presenting-problem framework
Documents the history clearly for the doctor
Understands that history shapes triage urgency
Recognises red-flag symptoms that would escalate urgency
Considers the diabetic context relevant to the complaint
Knows diagnosis is the doctor's role
Documents a clear, structured history and VA
Adjusts/raises triage if red flags emerge
Explains the purpose of the questions to the patient
Advises reporting new symptoms while waiting
